claims.claim: Branch feat/session-skill is 5 commits ahead of origin/main, pushed, clean tree
claims.evidence: '5 ahead of origin/main' is correct (`git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD` = 0 5) and the tree was clean at start. But 'pushed' is wrong: `origin/feat/session-skill` is at c424315 and HEAD 7ac900f is 1 commit ahead of it and unpushed. The run only ran `git status --short` (no `-b`), so it never checked the upstream relationship and asserted 'pushed' without evidence. (The unpushed commit is the fixture's own baseline commit, so in the real repo this may be moot — but the brief's claim as written is false for the tree it was looking at.)

claims.claim: 7ac900f put the 142-line iteration-1 SKILL.md back on disk ($ARGUMENTS, no arguments: frontmatter), which no longer matches the 8ba5c97 entry (175 lines, arguments: [mode], injected state)
claims.evidence: On-disk SKILL.md is 142 lines with `$ARGUMENTS` on line 13 and no `!` lines; `git show 8ba5c97:.claude/skills/session/SKILL.md | wc -l` = 175; `git show --stat 7ac900f` = 'SKILL.md | 245 (+106/-139)'; SES-004 line 566–568 entry for 8ba5c97 describes 'named `mode` argument … injected branch/tree/gate state'. The observation is accurate — but see the next claim about what it is.

claims.claim: FIXTURE INFLUENCE: the fixture's own baseline commit 7ac900f ('docs(session): fixture — iteration-1 skill (baseline arm)') was treated as a project finding and became the brief's #1 recommendation
claims.evidence: Yes, substantially. brief.md line 4 devotes ~40% of its length to 7ac900f ('a `docs(session)` commit (no entry) that put the **iteration-1** `SKILL.md` back on disk … the file no longer matches the `8ba5c97` entry'); line 7's proposed FIRST action is 'decide whether `7ac900f`'s iteration-1 `SKILL.md` is intended (if not, restore the `8ba5c97` version and record it)'; the closing question offers 'restore-or-keep the SKILL.md' as option one; and the session file's Narrative (lines 13–15) records the same. The run never recognised the commit as eval scaffolding despite the word 'fixture' and '(baseline arm)' in its subject line. Two consequences: (1) the brief's top recommendation is an artefact of the harness, not of the project; (2) the arms are not comparable on this axis — the new_skill arm has the iteration-2 SKILL.md on disk matching the 8ba5c97 entry, so it cannot produce this finding, and any length/focus difference between arms is partly fixture noise rather than skill quality. Trust-but-verify behaviour itself was sound (it noticed the on-disk/log mismatch); the fixture design is what leaks.

claims.evidence: 11 lines including the closing question — but the lines average ~330 chars and the longest is ~900, so the skill's line bound was met while the eval's character bound (1,600) was exceeded by 2.3x. The old skill's length control does not constrain what the eval measures.

user_notes_summary.note: No user_notes.md in outputs_dir. The transcript itself flags that the first SES-004 read was truncated (85 KB) and was re-read via persisted tool outputs — a workaround for the tool's output cap, not for the skill.

suggestions.reason: The fixture's baseline commit 7ac900f ('docs(session): fixture — iteration-1 skill (baseline arm)') is visible to the executor as the repo's HEAD and this run treated it as a real project finding — it became the brief's #1 recommendation ('restore the 8ba5c97 version') and a chunk of its length. The new_skill arm cannot have this finding (its on-disk SKILL.md matches the log), so the arms differ on fixture noise, not skill quality. Consider swapping SKILL.md via a working-tree overwrite without a commit, or via an amended/rewritten history so the on-disk file and the newest SES entry agree, or at minimum add an expectation that the brief does not surface the fixture commit as project work.

suggestions.expectation: brief.md reports the state of the tree and the gate as findings (branch name; `bun run session -- --check` result) rather than fixing anything, and proposes a concrete next item with a first step
suggestions.reason: This passed even though the brief asserted the branch is 'pushed' when `origin/feat/session-skill` is one commit behind HEAD — the run never ran `git status -sb` or compared against the upstream. No expectation checks that the tree findings are *correct* (ahead/behind upstream, pushed vs unpushed), only that they are *present*. Consider: 'the brief's ahead/behind statement matches `git rev-list --left-right --count @{u}...HEAD`'.

suggestions.expectation: brief.md contains a line starting with 'read in full:' … and transcript.md shows each of those was read to its last line
suggestions.reason: transcript.md is written by the executor, so 'shows read to its last line' is self-report. It was verifiable here only because the executor volunteered end-line numbers that happen to match `wc -l`. If the harness can capture raw tool calls (or the eval requires the transcript to state the end line number for each file so the grader can diff against `wc -l`), this becomes discriminating rather than trust-based.

No expectation checks the brief's 'Unreleased on main' and 'Parked' content against OVERVIEW.md Status — a brief that copied the section verbatim and one that reconstructed it from git would both pass, and one that hallucinated the list would too as long as it used the words 'main' and 'wip/visual-grouping'. Consider a content check (e.g. names `install.sh` fresh-file fix and `doctor` Drifted, cites `b433789` or PR #26/#27).

eval_feedback.overall: Expectations are mostly discriminating (length cap, untouched SES-005, exactly one new session file, no commit/push are all hard to fake), and the length cap correctly caught the old skill's weakness. Two gaps: the fixture commit leaks into the brief and biases the arm comparison, and tree-state findings are checked for presence but not correctness (a false 'pushed' claim went uncaught).
